ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory FINTRAC/PCMLTFA-compliant onboarding includes: (i) screening of all general partners, limited partners with a 25% or greater economic interest, ultimate beneficial owners and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, Canada's Domestic Sanctions List, and provincial enforcement lists; (ii) domestic and foreign PEP identification and enhanced due diligence in accordance with FINTRAC guidance; (iii) adverse-media and negative-news review; (iv) jurisdiction risk rating; and (v) ongoing transaction monitoring for the limited partnership's payment rails (Local_POS and Credit_Card). All screening results are documented in the AML/CFT onboarding file and retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Avis de réservation de nom / Enterprise Legal Publicity Registry online services portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c. C-11), the distinctive part of a Quebec enterprise name must be in French; a bilingual name may be accepted only if the French version is used in the enterprise's business and signage. Non-Latin-script names must be transliterated to Latin characters. The name must clearly indicate the limited partnership nature through a permitted suffix such as 'société en commandite', 'S.E.C.', 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.', according to the official language in which the name is filed.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 30 days of a written refusal from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, the applicant may file a reconsideration request with the RQ, attaching a revised name proposal, evidence of distinctiveness and any prior-use documents. If the RQ maintains the refusal, the applicant may appeal to the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) under the Act respecting legal publicity of enterprises and the Code of Civil Procedure. A further temporary name may be reserved while the appeal is pending, subject to RQ conditions.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or registered-agent address may satisfy the statutory service address requirement, but it is not acceptable to establish commercial substance for this specialty tea salon business. The operator must hold a commercial lease for an actual café/tea-lounge premises and obtain the municipal permits required for food and beverage service under ISIC 5630 / NAICS 722515.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High risk – approximately 75% probability of unannounced municipal food-safety and health inspection during the first six months of operation, plus possible Revenu Québec premises audit and local fire-safety inspection.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, Book Two, Title II, Chapter II (Sociétés en commandite), arts. 2236–2263; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c. P-44.1); Bank Act insolvency and partnership rules do not apply to provincial limited partnership registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Québec Enterprise Registrar), Enterprise Registration Service
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital contributions are fixed in the limited partnership agreement; no escrow account obligation is prescribed for a Quebec limited partnership.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the general partner approves the formation of the limited partnership and accepts the initial capital contributions recorded in the partnership register; that the registered office is fixed at the address shown in the Declaration of Registration and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is designated as filing authority; that the general partner be and is hereby appointed manager with authority to execute commercial agreements, open bank accounts, engage employees and obtain all permits required for the specialty tea salon lounge; and that all acts taken before this resolution are ratified as if done on behalf of the partnership. This resolution constitutes a valid governance action of the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online name reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search in the registrant's official name record through the Registraire's online portal; submit the application for name reservation in French or bilingual form using the proposed 'Specialty Tea Salon Lounge' denomination; pay the prescribed fee and obtain the name reservation certificate which is valid for 120 days.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation request
Name search report or waiver of search
Applicant identification
Proof of payment of the name reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, submit a revised name within the same application file or file a written review request; the Registraire offers a free rework window during the pending application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare Limited Partnership Agreement and Registration Data
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners and optional Quebec notary; internal governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société en commandite) in accordance with the Civil Code of Québec; record the general partner, limited partners, capital contributions, profit-sharing ratios and management authority; prepare the Declaration of Registration containing the partnership name, registered office address, partnership objects, and partner particulars.
required_dossiers: Signed limited partnership agreement
List of general and limited partners with capital contributions
Name reservation certificate
Consent to use registered office address in Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If internal documentation is incomplete, amend the agreement and registration data before filing; no penalty accrues if defects are cured prior to submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration electronically through the REQ online filing system or by mail to the registration office; include the prescribed partnership particulars, pay the registration fee, and obtain the enterprise number (NEQ) and the attestation d'immatriculation confirming the creation of the limited partnership.
required_dossiers: Completed Declaration of Registration
Executed limited partnership agreement retained for inspection
Name reservation certificate
Identification documents for general partner and partners
Registered office consent document
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire issues a request for additional information, respond within the prescribed delay; if the registration is refused, correct the material defect and refile with applicable fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Attestation, Tax Accounts, and Open Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and Revenu Québec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Download the attestation d'immatriculation and verify the legal form 'Société en commandite'; open a dedicated Quebec business bank account using the NEQ; register for GST/QST accounts with Revenu Québec if the partnership will make taxable supplies in Canada and Quebec.
required_dossiers: Attestation d'immatriculation
NEQ confirmation
Bank account opening forms for the partnership
GST/QST registration application (LM-1 and/or Revenu Québec form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax account registration is delayed, the partnership may rely on the federal and provincial registration thresholds and must register as soon as taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000 annually; assess the need for retroactive registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Initial Governance Filings and Annual Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec and municipal licensing office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place the partnership register at the registered office and record all partners, capital contributions, and management appointments; file the annual updating declaration (Déclaration annuelle) before the filing anniversary; notify the Registraire of any change in partners, registered office, or partnership name.
required_dossiers: Annual updating declaration
Partnership register of partners and contributions
Amendments to registration if changes occur
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the annual declaration is filed late, pay the late fee and file within the grace period; failure to notify changes may be cured by a declaration of amendment and payment of the prescribed penalty.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation (MAPAQ), Food Establishment Licensing Division; municipal zoning and building inspection services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Permis de restauration (Food Service Establishment Permit) for a specialty tea salon lounge; municipal commercial occupancy permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full environmental impact assessment; subject to municipal and provincial registration requirements where wastewater or residual materials handling exceeds commercial thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharges must meet municipal sewer-use standards and, where applicable, provincial industrial effluent criteria (Directive 019); commercial grease traps shall be installed for food and beverage service; volatile organic compound emissions from cleaning and tea packaging must remain below the provincial Clean Air Regulation registration thresholds; residual fats, oils and grease must be disposed of by a licensed carrier.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the municipal fire safety service verifying exits, extinguishers, and sprinkler requirements; building occupancy certificate issued after structural load inspection for ceramic amenities and furniture; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) occupational health clearance and emergency-protocol sign-off.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada, administered through the My Business Account portal (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Provincial (Quebec): Revenu Québec, administered through the CLIENT portal (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/en/), with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) as the corporate/legal registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident limited partnership carrying on business in Quebec must obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) from the CRA by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) online, by telephone, fax, or mail, and must open a GST/HST account coded RT. Concurrently, the société en commandite must register with Revenu Québec for the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) and, as a legal entity, must file an immatriculation with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, designating a natural person resident in Quebec as representative for service of documents and providing a fixed Quebec place of business for the tea salon lounge. The partnership itself, not the partners, becomes the GST/HST and QST registrant for the taxable business activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; a Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) is a legal person under the Civil Code of Québec but is fiscally transparent: no entity-level income tax applies and partners are taxed on their allocated shares. Available elections: (1) a partnership may elect to register for GST/HST and QST as a single registrant under Excise Tax Act s. 240(1) and the QST regime rather than having each partner register separately; (2) a non-calendar fiscal year-end election under Income Tax Act s. 96(12) for partnership years; (3) an allocation election under s. 96(5) ITA determining how partnership income/loss is distributed among partners; (4) under the Quebec Taxation Act, elections concerning the attribution of the establishment's taxable base between partners with a permanent establishment in Quebec; (5) anti-hybrid mismatch rules (ss. 18.4-18.6 ITA and equivalent QST provisions) restrict arrangements that would exploit partnership classifications between Canada and foreign jurisdictions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST) at 5% plus the Quebec Sales Tax (QST) at 9.975% imposed on the GST-included selling price, administered by Revenu Québec, yielding a combined headline VAT-type burden of 14.975% for on-premises taxable supplies in the specialty tea salon lounge.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 of worldwide taxable supplies (excluding capital assets) measured over four consecutive calendar quarters for small-supplier status under Excise Tax Act s. 148(1) and the QST Act; however, a non-resident limited partnership carrying on a business in Canada or making commercial supplies in the course of a business at a peace-officer-identified place in Quebec is generally required to register regardless of the threshold, and the tea salon with a physical lounge will normally exceed CAD 30,000 in sales, triggering mandatory registration from the first supply.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Quebec does not impose a continuous transaction control (CTC) electronic clearance, fiscal stamping, or mandatory API invoice-clearance regime comparable to Latin American jurisdictions. However, Revenu Québec mandates the use of a certified Sales Recording Module (SRM / module d'enregistrement des ventes) or a registered cash register system for operators of restaurant-type establishments, including tea salons serving beverages and prepared food for on-premises consumption, once annual gross turnover exceeds CAD 30,000; the SRM must record all sales transactions with digital integrity, and invoices must be produced in accordance with QST regulations. The CRA operates a voluntary e-invoicing pilot without any current statutory obligation for the federal GST accounts.

electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda._note: All supplies of tea beverages, pastry items, and lounge service are taxable at the full combined rate of 5% GST plus 9.975% QST; take-out sales of loose-leaf tea and packaged merchandise are also taxable at the same rate in Quebec.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The LP may zero-rate GST/HST and QST on supplies of tangible tea goods and cultural ceramic merchandise delivered to export markets when the goods are shipped by common carrier, mail, or courier to a foreign destination, provided the supplier retains proof that the goods were delivered outside Canada within the specified documentation window. Services supplied to a non-resident recipient (e.g., wholesale procurement brokerage, tea-culture consulting, or overseas event design performed from Quebec for foreign recipients who are not registered for GST/HST and are not present in Canada) are zero-rated under Schedule VI Part V s. 7 of the Excise Tax Act and corresponding QST rules, subject to carve-outs for services in connection with Canadian real property or performed on tangible personal property located in Canada for a recipient that is a consumer. Retail on-premises lounge sales to domestic customers do not qualify for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Export Declaration filed electronically through the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS) for shipments valued above CAD 2,000, or alternative carrier-generated proof of export for low-value parcels
Commercial invoice or sales contract evidencing the supply of tea goods/ceramics, the Canadian vendor (LP), the foreign buyer, and the consideration expressed in currency
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill naming a foreign consignee, foreign port or delivery address, and date of export, plus customs or carrier stamps showing departure from Canada
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/credit-card settlement record confirming receipt of proceeds from the foreign purchaser in a foreign or Canadian currency account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to intensive CRA and Revenu Québec audit scrutiny; if the exporter fails to produce the documentation bundle, the zero rating is reversed and unreported tax is assessed with interest. Civil penalties for false statements or omissions under Excise Tax Act s. 285 and QST equivalent amount to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the net tax, while gross negligence penalties may reach 50% of the net tax; criminal prosecution under Income Tax Act s. 239 can impose fines of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment up to five years. CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess beyond the standard four-year limitation period where misrepresentation, neglect, or fraud is established, and retroactive clawbacks apply to the full amount of zero-rated refunds plus interest compounded daily; records must be retained for six years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), established under the Bank of Canada Act. Foreign exchange administration in Canada is decentralized: the Department of Finance Canada oversees sanctions and trade policies; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises federally authorized financial institutions; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) enforces cross-border transaction reporting and AML/ATF obligations. No single Canadian FX-control authority exists and no central bank approval is required for ordinary capital or current account transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar is fully convertible. Canada maintains no general foreign exchange controls, and neither current account payments (tea inventory imports, service fees, royalties) nor capital account transactions (capital contributions, distributions, profit remittances by non-resident limited partners) require Bank of Canada authorization. Practical hurdles are limited to AML/KYC onboarding, CRS/FATCA beneficial ownership documentation, Quebec civil-law notarial requirements, and, for payments to non-resident partners, Part XIII non-resident withholding under the Income Tax Act (normally 25% unless reduced by treaty, reported on NR4 forms). Profit remittance is lawful, but the corporate treasury must classify remittances as partnership distributions rather than salary or royalty to avoid over-withholding and preserve capital account integrity.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no mandatory surrender or forced conversion of export proceeds. Exporters may retain receivables in USD, EUR, CNY, or other currencies and may operate foreign-denominated bank accounts. There is no statutory timeline for repatriation or conversion. For Canadian tax accounting, Section 261 of the Income Tax Act requires foreign currency amounts to be translated into Canadian dollars using the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate, or an acceptable alternative rate, at the time income is recognized. GST/HST zero-rating for qualifying exports does not displace the recordkeeping requirement.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary payment rail, Low as a sole treasury solution. Offshore digital EMIs, including fintech platforms with multi-currency virtual accounts, may support inbound remittance collection and low-value supplier disbursements, but they are not members of Payments Canada and cannot provide Lynx/ACSS clearing, CRA payroll tax debits, or fully compliant Quebec payroll infrastructure. Legal constraints arise under the Bank Act, which reserves deposit-taking and payments in Canada for authorized institutions; an EMI acting as a money-services business must be registered with FINTRAC and may require provincial licensing from the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) in Quebec. Use EMIs only for pre-funded, low-value cross-border payments; the primary operational and capital accounts must remain with a Schedule I Canadian bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required in practice. FINTRAC permits remote identity verification using defined mechanisms, but large Schedule I banks commonly require at least one in-person signing at a Quebec commercial branch for a non-resident-owned limited partnership. Directors and ultimate beneficial owners can complete documentary KYC remotely if their identity documents are certified, and a Quebec-resident authorized signatory may open the account on behalf of the general partner; however, most tier-1 banks expect the general partner or a director with signing authority to attend a face-to-face interview if the partnership has non-resident partners. The bank will independently search the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, verify the partnership's matricule, and require original formation documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear general partner authority or inconsistent Quebec LP registration
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized partnership agreement; certificate of registration from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec; declaration of the general partner; unanimous resolution of the general partner authorizing account opening and designated signatories; corporate registry extracts of the general partner; current Quebec business address and lease agreement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident partners causing beneficial ownership opacity or sanction-list hits
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial ownership chart showing every partner holding 25% or more; passports and residence proofs; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; OSFI/FINTRAC-compliant CDD questionnaires; CRS/FATCA self-certifications; independent professional references; sanctions screening explanations where any name partially matches.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy tea salon/retail operations triggering structured-deposit suspicion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Point-of-sale transaction logs, daily sales reconciliation summaries, cash-handling and cash-in-transit contracts, register closeout procedures, inventory and wastage records, monthly accountant-reviewed financial statements, and the partnership's written AML/ATF policy and employee training register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border capital injection mismatched with stated capital contribution or loan purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: LP capital account ledger and contribution schedule referencing the partnership agreement; legal purpose declaration in SWIFT remittance information; foreign exchange transaction receipts; regulatory tax filings confirming the injection is capital and not income; bank reference letters from the remitting bank; notarized statutory declarations from contributing partners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use direct SWIFT MT103 messaging from the partner's foreign bank to the receiving Schedule I Canadian bank account held in the exact legal name of the Quebec limited partnership. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must state 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — [Legal Name of Partner] to [Legal Name of LP]' and reference the relevant partnership agreement article. The receiving bank will map the payment to an internal purpose code for FINTRAC EFT reporting if the amount exceeds CAD 10,000. No Bank of Canada permit is required. For USD or other foreign currencies, use the receiving bank's spot FX desk or pre-agreed standing instruction; for CAD, route through SWIFT correspondent clearing or Lynx. The treasury must deliver the full source-of-funds evidence package to the receiving bank before settlement to avoid hold/rejection.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier invoices for loose-leaf tea and ceramic products should be settled using SWIFT MT103 wires for high-value overseas vendors. Large or shipment-based trade may use commercial letters of credit or documentary collections issued by a Schedule I Canadian bank. Domestic disbursements should use Payments Canada ACSS (EFTs/ACH debits) for routine GST/HST, payroll, utilities, and retail vendor payments; urgent large transactions should use Lynx, Canada's high-value real-time settlement system. Every FX conversion must be supported by a bank treasury ticket noting counterparty, rate, notional, and purpose. Non-resident royalty, management fee, or distribution payments must be separately classified; royalties and rents paid to non-residents require Part XIII withholding, reporting through CRA forms NR4, and settlement via a bank wire carrying the correct tax reference.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign exchange forward contracts executed with a Canadian Schedule I bank or licensed investment dealer
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies lacking active domestic deliverable markets, provided the counterparty is a qualifying dealer and the hedge purpose is documented
Cross-currency interest rate swaps matching the LP's foreign supplier payables or partner capital repayment exposures
Plain-vanilla purchased FX options for tea import cost protection, subject to bank credit approval and derivative documentation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Enterprise Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle de mise à jour) filed under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (RLRQ c. P-44.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Registrar of Quebec Enterprises, REQ)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the anniversary date of the limited partnership's registration in the Quebec enterprise register; a registration anniversary of January 1 results in a filing deadline of March 31 of the same year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The registrar issues a notice and, if the declaration remains unfiled, may cancel the declaration of registration after a 45-day cure period; the LP is then administratively struck off the register and cannot lawfully operate in Quebec, and limited partners may lose the liability shield against third parties until the registration is restored.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013) and T5013 Summary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), Partnership Income Tax Section
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than five months after the end of the partnership's fiscal period; for a fiscal year ending December 31, the return is due by May 31 of the following calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalties accrue at CAD 25 per partner per day, up to a maximum of CAD 2,500 per partnership; continued non-compliance can trigger CRA compliance measures, gross negligence penalties, and prosecution under the Income Tax Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Quebec limited partnerships are not required by law to obtain an independent audit solely because of LP status. A mandatory audit is triggered only when the LP is a reporting issuer under Quebec securities law, when the partnership agreement or a unanimous partner agreement requires an audited financial statement, when the general partner is itself a reporting issuer consolidating the LP, or when a lender or regulator imposes an audit as a condition of financing or licensing.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: A private Quebec limited partnership may prepare financial statements under Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, CPA Canada Handbook Part II); IFRS is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises and is otherwise permitted but not required. Tax income is computed in accordance with the federal Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec does not require a separate UBO annual return for a limited partnership. The annual enterprise declaration identifies the general partners and certain enterprise information, but it does not constitute a full beneficial-ownership confirmation. On each transfer of a limited partnership interest, the partnership ledger and capital account records must be updated, and the annual anti-money-laundering/KYC file identifying individuals ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of partnership interests must be refreshed and retained by the registered office or designated agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: No statutory register of members or directors is prescribed for a Quebec limited partnership itself; the partnership record book containing the limited partnership agreement, capital contribution ledger, resolutions of partners, and powers of attorney must be kept at the principal establishment.

If the general partner is a corporation incorporated under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, that corporate general partner must maintain at its registered office the statutory registers required by that Act, including the register of directors, register of shareholders, and minute book.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 to CAD 750 annually (approximately USD 190 to USD 550) for a licensed registered-office service provider in Quebec, plus CAD 150 to CAD 400 for KYC/UBO recordkeeping and annual declaration preparation.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 to USD 12,000 for a full ASPE audit of a specialty tea salon LP with annual revenue below CAD 1.5 million; a review engagement typically ranges from USD 1,900 to USD 3,800.

stage_6.entry_description: Legal name, registered office, Business Number (BN), fiscal period end, entity class (Quebec society en commandite / LP), jurisdiction of formation.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter foreign partner's country of residence; if the LP has no Canadian address, list the GP's business address and the Canadian resident agent.
